parts.name: casting

physics.Basic_description: The main black body of the plane, appearing as a heavy, matte-finished cast metal structure with a flat sole and raised sides.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the structural backbone and weight for the tool, holding all other components in alignment.
physics.Grasped_description: A robot gripper would grasp the side walls or the top surface of the casting to lift or stabilize the entire tool.
physics.reason: Cast iron plane bodies are thin-walled shells with internal ribbing and empty space to reduce weight while maintaining rigidity; treating the bounding box as solid iron would vastly overestimate mass.

parts.description: The main black body of the plane, appearing as a heavy, matte-finished cast metal structure with a flat sole and raised sides.
parts.function: Provides the structural backbone and weight for the tool, holding all other components in alignment.

parts.name: sole edge

physics.Basic_description: A thin green strip at the very bottom of the plane body, representing the machined sole surface.
physics.Functional_description: The flat reference surface that slides against the workpiece to ensure a smooth cut.
physics.Grasped_description: Not intended for grasping; it is the contact surface with the workpiece.
physics.reason: This represents the machined bottom face of the casting, which is effectively a solid layer of material at the contact point.

parts.description: A thin green strip at the very bottom of the plane body, representing the machined sole surface.
parts.function: The flat reference surface that slides against the workpiece to ensure a smooth cut.

parts.name: frog

physics.Basic_description: A blue-colored angled block seated within the body casting, supporting the blade assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Holds the cutting iron at the correct angle (typically 45 degrees) relative to the sole.
physics.Grasped_description: Located internally and obstructed by the blade; not a primary grasp point.
physics.reason: The frog is typically a solid or heavily ribbed cast block designed to resist flexing under cutting pressure.

parts.description: A blue-colored angled block seated within the body casting, supporting the blade assembly.
parts.function: Holds the cutting iron at the correct angle (typically 45 degrees) relative to the sole.

parts.name: depth stud

physics.Basic_description: A small yellow cylindrical post visible near the adjustment mechanism.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as a pivot or stop for the depth adjustment lever.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and recessed to be a useful grasp point.
physics.reason: Small mechanical studs and pins are solid metal components.

parts.description: A small yellow cylindrical post visible near the adjustment mechanism.
parts.function: Acts as a pivot or stop for the depth adjustment lever.

parts.name: cap post

physics.Basic_description: A small orange component, likely part of the lever cap retention mechanism.
physics.Functional_description: Secures the lever cap which holds the blade down against the frog.
physics.Grasped_description: Not suitable for grasping due to size and function.
physics.reason: Fasteners and posts in this context are solid metal.

parts.description: A small orange component, likely part of the lever cap retention mechanism.
parts.function: Secures the lever cap which holds the blade down against the frog.

parts.name: iron

physics.Basic_description: A purple/silver angled rectangular plate with a sharp edge, resting on the frog.
physics.Functional_description: The actual blade that cuts the wood; adjustable for depth of cut.
physics.Grasped_description: Could be grasped by the top edge for removal or adjustment, though sharp.
physics.reason: Plane blades are solid plates of hardened steel, typically 2-3mm thick.

parts.description: A purple/silver angled rectangular plate with a sharp edge, resting on the frog.
parts.function: The actual blade that cuts the wood; adjustable for depth of cut.

parts.name: nut

physics.Basic_description: A small cyan circular knob or nut on the lever cap assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Used to tighten or loosen the lever cap to secure the blade.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper could pinch this to rotate and adjust the cap tension.
physics.reason: Nuts and knobs of this size are solid metal.

parts.description: A small cyan circular knob or nut on the lever cap assembly.
parts.function: Used to tighten or loosen the lever cap to secure the blade.

parts.name: tote

physics.Basic_description: A large pink vertical handle at the rear of the plane, shaped ergonomically for gripping.
physics.Functional_description: The primary handle for the user's dominant hand to push and control the plane.
physics.Grasped_description: The most natural grasp point for lifting or moving the tool; gripper would enclose the handle.
physics.reason: Rear totes are solid pieces of hardwood carved for grip.

parts.description: A large pink vertical handle at the rear of the plane, shaped ergonomically for gripping.
parts.function: The primary handle for the user's dominant hand to push and control the plane.

parts.name: lever

physics.Basic_description: A lime green thin lever arm visible near the blade assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Adjusts the lateral tilt of the blade to ensure the cut is parallel to the sole.
physics.Grasped_description: Too thin and small for a stable grasp; manipulated by finger tips.
physics.reason: Levers are solid stamped or machined steel strips.

parts.description: A lime green thin lever arm visible near the blade assembly.
parts.function: Adjusts the lateral tilt of the blade to ensure the cut is parallel to the sole.

parts.name: wheel

physics.Basic_description: A teal/yellow knurled wheel located at the rear of the blade assembly.
physics.Functional_description: Rotated to raise or lower the blade for adjusting the depth of cut.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper could pinch the edges of the wheel to rotate it for adjustment.
physics.reason: Adjustment wheels are solid machined brass or bronze components.

parts.description: A teal/yellow knurled wheel located at the rear of the blade assembly.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
